A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VDLM/PVD research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-G support reliable comparison despite retitling and reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original zero-shot evaluations on nine downstream tasks, SVG-versus-image experiments, linear probing, and perception/reasoning error analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds multimodal VDLM evaluations, VGBench-QA results, reasoner comparisons, and an augmentation ablation.

M1.justification: Section 2.3 adds VDLM-mm, which supplies the original image alongside PVD to a multimodal reasoner; the earlier method becomes VDLM-txt. This extends inference inputs while retaining VTracer, SVG decomposition, the PVD ontology, and SVG-to-PVD training.

E1.justification: v4 adds rasterized VGBench-QA images with Category, Color, and Usage questions. This substantially broadens evaluation from precise geometric and spatial reasoning to semantic identification and knowledge about graphic usage. The earlier downstream and probing tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-4o and G-LLaVA-7b to the original nine-task comparison, introducing a stronger general comparator and a geometry-specialized model. G-LLaVA was cited but not evaluated there in v3. Existing LLaVA, GPT-4V, and ViperGPT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce four-option VGBench-QA evaluation on 100 sampled instances per category, comparisons with and without PVD across multimodal reasoners, and an augmentation control. Existing task sample counts, zero-shot evaluation, and SVG-to-PVD training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 examines how PVD benefits vary across reasoners, including LLaVA-based variants. Appendix C adds an ablation of Gaussian blur and pixel noise, which were already training components in v3. The earlier correlation, probing, and error analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The versions retain the same regression/KDE analyses and ten-epoch probing averages. v4 introduces no repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: New comparisons report GPT-4o image-only/VDLM-mm accuracy of 0.663/0.769 on low-level tasks and 0.726/0.743 on VGBench-QA. Table 5 adds augmentation results, including DINOv2 scores of 0.874 without augmentation and 0.893 with it. Retained Table 1 results are unchanged apart from rounding.

T1.justification: The PVD primitive definitions and language-modeling objective in Equation 1 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, mathematical results, derivations, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the contribution from text-only reasoning through PVD to directly augmenting existing multimodal reasoners. The core claims about task-agnostic visual descriptions, zero-shot generalization, and interpretability remain.

C2.justification: v4 interprets PVD benefits as dependent on sufficiently capable reasoners and discusses how imperfect perception can hurt GPT-4o on Shapeworld tasks. The conclusion shifts emphasis from SVG's representational limitations to the learned SVG-to-PVD module and its restricted ontology.

D1.justification: v4 supplies the GPT-4o version identifier and VGBench-QA prompts, and documents image-plus-PVD prompting. Training hardware, hyperparameters, augmentation settings, and project access remain unchanged. The v3 note that code-execution failures count as incorrect is removed.

R1.justification: v4 expands discussion of SVG generation and understanding with works including StarVector, StrokeNUWA, VectorPainter, and VGBench, and adds web/OS-agent motivation. HallusionBench and two code-agent references are removed. The established related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, and the abstract, introduction, and results narrative are extensively rewritten around two research questions and the text-only/multimodal distinction. Section 3 gains explicit Tasks, Models, and Results subsections, with substantial accompanying language revisions.

P2.justification: v4 revises the framework diagrams, expands Figure 4, regroups Table 1, and adds a reasoner-comparison figure, high-level results table, augmentation table, and prompt figure. Typography changes throughout, and retained appendix displays are reflowed and relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through comparisons using the same multimodal reasoner with and without PVD, high-level QA evaluation, and targeted reasoner and augmentation analyses. These clarify where PVD helps and where limitations remain. This is a useful extension of an already substantial empirical study; small evaluation subsets and absent uncertainty estimates persist, while removal of the code-execution-error scoring note slightly weakens reproducibility.
